summary: Good news if you live in New York City: we checked, and a pet rat is allowed. NYC's famously strict Health Code (Article 161, Section 161.01) bans a long list of wild animals, including 'all large rodents' such as gopher, muskrat, beaver, prairie dog, and capybara, plus squirrels and bats. But that list targets large and wild rodents, not small domesticated ones. A pet rat (like the common fancy rat that New Yorkers already keep) is a small domesticated rodent and is not on the prohibited list. A pet roof rat is allowed, the same as New York State. Selling rats commercially at retail needs a DOHMH Class P pet-shop permit; keeping one, or placing or giving one away privately, needs no permit.

keep.why: NYC Health Code Section 161.01 ('Wild and other animals prohibited') lists prohibited species including, at item (14), 'all large rodents (Rodentia), including, but not limited to, gopher, muskrat, nutria, paca, woodchuck, marmot, beaver, prairie dog, capybara, sewellel, viscacha, porcupine and hutia,' plus all squirrels and all bats. Small domesticated rodents (the common pet rat, mouse, hamster, gerbil, guinea pig) are not on that list and are kept as pets throughout the city. A domesticated roof rat is a small rodent, not a 'large rodent' or wild animal, so it is not prohibited. Not stricter than New York State.
keep.governing_law: NYC Health Code Article 161, Section 161.01 (Wild and Other Animals Prohibited; item 14 bans large rodents, not small domesticated rodents).

breed.why: No local rodent-breeding restriction; the state's permissive rule applies.

sell_give.why: In New York City, commercial retail sale of rats requires a Class P 'Pet Shop' permit from DOHMH (NYC Health Code §161.09; ch. 5), the same permit documented on the parent New York page. Rats remain sellable in NYC even after Local Law 132 (2024) banned the retail sale of dogs, cats, guinea pigs, and rabbits. Private, face-to-face placement and giveaways need no permit.
sell_give.governing_law: NYC Health Code §161.09 & ch. 5 (Class P pet-shop permit; Local Law 132/2024); see New York (state) for the statewide framework.

transport.why: No local transport restriction on a pet rat; the state's rule applies.

restrictions.summary: In New York City, a commercial retail seller of rats needs a Class P 'Pet Shop' permit from DOHMH (facility inspections; integrated pest management). Rats remain legally sellable in NYC even after Local Law 132 (2024) banned the retail sale of dogs, cats, guinea pigs, and rabbits. Private/face-to-face placement and giveaways need no permit.
steps: If running an NYC retail storefront, obtain a DOHMH Class P pet-shop permit
